rows.rationale: Germany most clearly converts a technical ODD into a public-law deployment object: lawful autonomous operation is geographically bounded by an approved operating area.
rows.regulatory_object: Autonomous vehicle + approved defined operating area + keeper + technical supervision
rows.technical_baseline: EU/UNECE technical baseline plus German autonomous-vehicle operating permit under StVG/AFGBV
rows.deployment_gate: Vehicle operating permit + authority approval of defined operating area + registration before autonomous road use
rows.odd_legalisation: ODD is translated into a geographically defined and authority-approved 'festgelegter Betriebsbereich'
rows.authority: KBA / competent road authority depending on decision layer
rows.accountable_actor: Halter (vehicle keeper), with manufacturer duties and Technische Aufsicht functions separately allocated
rows.remote_role: Technische Aufsicht – may deactivate and release specified manoeuvres; not ordinary continuous remote driving
rows.ddt_allocation: ADS performs DDT; system must comply with road rules and achieve minimum-risk condition where necessary
rows.offence_allocation: Dedicated AV behavioural architecture; legal duties are distributed among ADS framework, keeper and supervisor rather than simply retained by an onboard driver
rows.civil_liability: General StVG keeper-liability / insurance architecture remains central; not wholly replaced by AV-specific civil liability
rows.data_logging: Statutory event/data duties; AFGBV data-storage requirements
rows.in_use_oversight: KBA/authority market surveillance and permit supervision
rows.material_change: AFGBV § 4(5) expressly requires KBA approval before post-permit changes to an autonomous vehicle are used; § 6 allows withdrawal/suspension of the vehicle operating permit where approval conditions cease to be met.
rows.revalidation: Explicit lifecycle control: KBA approval for vehicle changes; suspension/withdrawal pending clarification under § 6; operating-area approval can be suspended/withdrawn under § 10 when safety assumptions or infrastructure conditions cease to hold.
rows.service_pathway: Possible within approved operating area and applicable transport/service law

rows.rationale: France regulates the socio-technical transport system, not merely the vehicle. Technical approval is necessary but not sufficient for service deployment.
rows.regulatory_object: Automated road transport system: vehicle + technical system + route/zone + service organisation
rows.technical_baseline: EU type approval / relevant vehicle technical approval
rows.deployment_gate: Prior system safety demonstration + qualified independent opinions + formal mise-en-service decision
rows.odd_legalisation: Safety case is tied to intended route or zone and service configuration
rows.authority: Service organiser / competent transport and road authorities within statutory framework
rows.accountable_actor: Automated transport-system/service operator architecture rather than vehicle owner alone
rows.remote_role: Qualified remote intervention personnel integrated into system operation
rows.ddt_allocation: ADS performs DDT; remote intervention supports defined situations without collapsing into ordinary remote driving
rows.offence_allocation: Dedicated criminal-responsibility adaptations exist; detailed allocation depends on operating mode and legal actor
rows.civil_liability: Compulsory insurance/general civil-liability rules supplemented by dedicated automated-driving responsibility provisions; civil layer less comprehensive than deployment layer
rows.data_logging: System/event recording and safety-management evidence required
rows.in_use_oversight: In-use system safety management and authority oversight tied to service operation
rows.material_change: Code des transports R3151-1 defines a substantial modification as one that changes the safety assessment; R3152-18 requires notification and, for a substantially modified system, suspension of operation.
rows.revalidation: Explicit re-commissioning: after a substantial modification the organiser suspends operation and a new mise-en-service decision is taken under R3152-10 to R3152-12; R3152-11 applies to new or substantially modified systems.
rows.service_pathway: Yes. Passenger automated-road-transport-system pathway extended to automated road freight by Décret 2024-1063, effective 28 Nov 2024.
rows.primary_source_anchor: Ordonnance 2021-443; Décret 2021-873; Code des transports R3151/R3152; Décret 2024-1063 / R3251–R3253

rows.rationale: Croatia is especially useful for the bridge from EU type approval to local service validation in real operating conditions.
rows.regulatory_object: Fully automated vehicle + owner + operating area + transport service + remote intervention arrangements
rows.deployment_gate: Dedicated road-traffic rules plus mandatory real-world service validation before passenger-service deployment
rows.odd_legalisation: Operating area / territory forms part of deployment validation and service conditions
rows.authority: Transport/road authorities; licensing authority under national transport framework
rows.accountable_actor: Vehicle owner is a central road-traffic accountability actor; service operator duties exist at transport layer
rows.remote_role: Remote intervention role recognised; boundaries and concurrency remain implementation questions
rows.ddt_allocation: ADS performs driverless operation; remote intervention supports defined operational/safety functions
rows.offence_allocation: Owner bears dedicated responsibility for traffic offences of fully automated vehicle in driverless operation
rows.civil_liability: Traffic-offence allocation is clear; broader AV-specific civil-liability architecture is less complete
rows.data_logging: Strong telemetry/event-data access and video-surveillance duties
rows.in_use_oversight: Service/deployment oversight, incident management and licence conditions
rows.material_change: Partial change-control only: a new special-conditions certificate is required within 15 days if certificate data change; general testing applies to converted/modified vehicle hardware under Road Safety Act Art 276.
rows.revalidation: No equally explicit rule located that a material ADS/ODD/software/service change automatically re-triggers the Art 13b–13d real-world service-validation procedure. Serious incidents can trigger temporary prohibition of a FAV type under Art 290a.
rows.service_pathway: Yes, through transport licensing after service-level real-world validation
rows.primary_source_anchor: NN 145/2024 Arts 281a–281f; NN 154/2024 Arts 13b–13d / Art 51a framework

rows.rationale: UK is a control case showing that actor/institution design can legally precede full ordinary deployment.
rows.regulatory_object: APS permit holder and pilot-operator architecture as the 2026 transitional route; authorised self-driving vehicle / responsible-entity architecture enacted but not yet commenced
rows.technical_baseline: UK vehicle approval/self-driving authorisation architecture under AV Act implementation programme
rows.deployment_gate: Automated Passenger Service permit under Part 5 of the AV Act 2024 (in force 15 May 2026) for eligible passenger services; other deployments run as pilots under vehicle special orders; Part 1 authorisation not yet commenced at snapshot
rows.odd_legalisation: Deployment area fixed through APS permit and pilot conditions; authorised domain under Part 1 of the AV Act not yet in force
rows.authority: Secretary of State / DVSA and relevant local transport authority for APS consent
rows.accountable_actor: APS permit holder / pilot operator; ASDE and NUiC-operator architecture in Part 1 of the AV Act not yet in force
rows.remote_role: No German-style technical supervisor as universal core role; remote functions depend on operating model
rows.ddt_allocation: Authorised ADS performs self-driving task; user-in-charge duties are separated where relevant
rows.offence_allocation: No general rule in force at snapshot: Part 1 reallocation of legal responsibility away from the user not yet commenced; pilot and permit conditions require reporting of infractions
rows.civil_liability: Dedicated: Automated and Electric Vehicles Act 2018 s. 2 makes the insurer liable for accidents caused by a listed automated vehicle driving itself; AV Act 2024 insurance and liability provisions pending
rows.data_logging: Reporting under APS permit conditions and pilot conditions (collisions, infractions); information duties of Part 1 of the AV Act not yet in force
rows.in_use_oversight: Oversight through APS permit monitoring and pilot conditions; in-use regulation under Part 1 planned for full implementation
rows.material_change: APS Regulations 2026 treat a material change in circumstances as a ground for permit variation, suspension or withdrawal; AV Act ss 5, 8 and 9 authorisation powers not yet commenced
rows.revalidation: Permit-level: variation, suspension or withdrawal of an APS permit or pilot on breach or incident; general authorisation lifecycle under Part 1 remains implementation-stage through 2027
rows.service_pathway: APS permit enables staged commercial passenger deployment in 2026
rows.dominant_model: Staged-permit model (APS permits and pilots ahead of Part 1 authorisation)
rows.legal_status: Partly in force: Part 5 (APS permits) from 15 May 2026; Part 1 authorisation and Part 4 marketing restrictions commence in 2027
rows.primary_source_anchor: Automated Vehicles Act 2024 and Commencement No. 1–3 Regulations (SI 2025/1339, 2026/437, 2026/731); SI 2026/439; AEVA 2018 s. 2; DfT implementation programme

rows.rationale: China already demonstrates the second-gate logic in practice even before the new national Road Traffic Safety Law is enacted.
rows.regulatory_object: Conditionally admitted L3 vehicle + designated user entity + specified roads/speeds + road-access pilot
rows.technical_baseline: Conditional product admission; GB 44721-2026 adopted but effective from 1 July 2027
rows.deployment_gate: Product admission is followed by geographically/functionally limited road-access pilot rather than unrestricted deployment
rows.odd_legalisation: Specified road segments, speed limits and operating conditions function as legally bounded ODD/geofence
rows.authority: MIIT and participating local authorities under pilot framework
rows.accountable_actor: Designated user entity + manufacturer within monitored pilot architecture
rows.remote_role: No mature national standalone technical-supervisor/remote-operator role architecture yet
rows.ddt_allocation: L3 ADS performs DDT within approved conditions; human fallback remains relevant to L3 design
rows.offence_allocation: Current pilot arrangements do not yet equal the proposed national manufacturer-centric offence rule
rows.civil_liability: Existing compulsory insurance/general rules apply; national AV-specific insurance provisions are proposed, not yet enacted
rows.data_logging: Pilot monitoring and safety evidence required
rows.in_use_oversight: Government monitoring and conditional product/road-access controls
rows.material_change: Pilot/product approval is version- and condition-sensitive; exact general change-control rule is still evolving
rows.revalidation: Road-access pilots and reassessment provide staged evidence before expansion
rows.service_pathway: Limited pilot deployment; not unrestricted nationwide commercial L3 operation
rows.legal_status: In force as pilot / conditional admission architecture
rows.primary_source_anchor: MIIT conditional L3 approvals of 15 Dec 2025; GB 44721-2026

rows.regime_label: China – 2026 Road Traffic Safety Law draft
rows.rationale: Analytically important but must not be coded as current Chinese law. It adds a national road-use layer to the already emerging technical and pilot layers.
rows.regulatory_object: Autonomous vehicle/ADS + manufacturer/importer + road-use accountability layer
rows.technical_baseline: Road-traffic-rule conformity test + technical/product admission; GB 44721-2026 technical pillar
rows.deployment_gate: Registered AV may activate ADS only within design operating conditions; national road-use rules sit above technical conformity
rows.odd_legalisation: Manufacturer/importer must ensure ADS cannot activate outside design operating conditions
rows.authority: Public-security / product / transport authorities under State Council allocation
rows.accountable_actor: Manufacturer/importer becomes direct central accountability actor for ADS-active traffic violations
rows.remote_role: Remote human role remains underdeveloped in the draft
rows.ddt_allocation: ADS continuously performs full DDT within design operating conditions; L2 assistance is expressly distinguished
rows.offence_allocation: Manufacturer/importer 'accepts handling' for violation while ADS active and bears burden of proof if claiming it was unrelated to ADS
rows.civil_liability: Compulsory motor-vehicle liability insurance required; commercial insurance encouraged; detailed regime delegated
rows.data_logging: Strong accident evidence/data duties and manufacturer data-provision obligations
rows.in_use_oversight: National road-safety risk assessment can support suspension/prohibition, recall, repair, replacement/refund/compensation measures
rows.material_change: Unauthorised ADS modification prohibited and sanctioned; post-market risk layer is explicit
rows.revalidation: Implementing rules still required; change/revalidation mechanics not fully specified
rows.service_pathway: Supports ordinary national road operation once enacted and implementing rules exist
rows.primary_source_anchor: Road Traffic Safety Law revision draft Arts 95–103

rows.rationale: The central inter-layer gap remains: technical admissibility does not yet map onto a general legal route for commercial driverless deployment.
rows.regulatory_object: EU-approved vehicle + national test-operation / narrower operational exceptions
rows.technical_baseline: EU/UNECE type-approval framework can provide high technical maturity
rows.deployment_gate: Predominantly § 49 test-operation permit; the only non-test deployment gate is the operational permit for automated delivery vehicles under § 52 of Act 106/2018; no general dedicated commercial FAV deployment gate
rows.odd_legalisation: ODD reflected in permit/test conditions; for automated delivery vehicles the operational permit fixes territory, route and time (§ 52(6)); not yet a general autonomous-operation authorisation object
rows.authority: Ministry of Transport / road and police authorities depending on permit
rows.accountable_actor: Permit holder / owner / driver-type roles; operator holding an operational permit for automated delivery vehicles (§ 52); no general licensed FAV operator architecture in force
rows.remote_role: No general commercial FAV technical-supervision/control-centre role in force; supervising driver (dohliadajúci vodič) with remote takeover for automated delivery vehicles (Act 8/2009 § 2(2)(w), § 5(6))
rows.ddt_allocation: Current framework remains structurally driver/test oriented; dedicated driverless DDT allocation is incomplete
rows.offence_allocation: No complete general rule for traffic offences committed by driverless FAV
rows.civil_liability: General motor insurance/civil liability; no mature FAV-specific allocation
rows.data_logging: Test-operation documentation and technical rules; supervision log and permit-conditioned operational data for automated delivery vehicles (Act 8/2009 § 6(7); Act 106/2018 § 52(6)–(7)); no general FAV logging architecture equivalent to CPT 1329
rows.in_use_oversight: Primarily permit/test supervision rather than mature in-use driverless market oversight
rows.material_change: Handled through technical approval/test permit changes; no general deployment change-control regime
rows.revalidation: Retesting tied mainly to test-operation context
rows.service_pathway: No general pathway from EU type approval to ordinary commercial driverless operation; goods delivery by automated delivery vehicles is the only permitted service use (Act 8/2009 § 55b; Act 106/2018 § 52)
rows.primary_source_anchor: Act 106/2018 §§ 49, 52; Act 8/2009 §§ 2, 5, 6, 55b; Decree 131/2018; Act 131/2026 effective 1 Sep 2026 only prospectively at snapshot

rows.rationale: The draft is conceptually close to a mature second-gate architecture, but actor boundaries, offence allocation, material-change control and the relation between licence and operation approval should be tightened.
rows.regulatory_object: Licensed FAV operator + approved operation + control centre + supervision operator + ODD
rows.deployment_gate: Operator licence + specific operation approval would create a genuine second gate
rows.odd_legalisation: ODD and defined roads/territory become part of operational documentation / approval
rows.authority: Ministry of Transport with police/other authority inputs
rows.accountable_actor: Licensed FAV operator becomes organisational centre of responsibility
rows.remote_role: Operátor dohľadu + riadiace centrum; current draft boundary with remote driving needs correction
rows.ddt_allocation: ADS should remain DDT performer; current wording risks transferring DDT remotely to supervisor in some clauses
rows.offence_allocation: Still requires explicit rule for offences committed by FAV while ADS is active
rows.civil_liability: Insurance/organisational requirements improve, but full civil/product/service allocation remains to be clarified
rows.in_use_oversight: Operator/licence supervision and operational duties create stronger in-use layer
rows.material_change: Draft requires clearer material-change / software-version triggers
rows.revalidation: Local validation/testing is structurally present but should be proportionate and recognise existing type-approval/foreign evidence
rows.service_pathway: Potential general commercial pathway if enacted and separated from test-only logic

purpose: Comparative model of the legal gate between technical vehicle/ADS approval and lawful real-world deployment. Current law and draft/prospective regimes are separated. Snapshot: 31 August 2026.
